# InfraBench

> InfraBench is the benchmark for **infrastructure agents**: it evaluates AI agents on realistic infrastructure incidents across the full system stack and the full operational lifecycle, with fine-grained risk assessment. Published at HotInfra '26 (co-located with ISCA '26). Maintained by researchers at the University of Wisconsin–Madison and Iowa State University.

InfraBench exists because coding benchmarks do not predict operational competence: an agent that passes SWE-bench can still take down production. Twelve seed tasks span hardware and BMC/IPMI recovery (L1), local systems and block-device work (L2), distributed systems such as Cassandra and Ceph (L3), and user-facing applications and data recovery (L4). Tasks run against real backends — Docker containers, KVM virtual machines, multi-node VM clusters, and bare-metal CloudLab hardware — rather than mocks.

Scoring goes beyond binary pass/fail. Task verifiers report structured checks covering whether the service actually recovered, whether the fix survived a restart (durability), whether system invariants held, whether collateral damage was avoided (risk), and whether the environment was left clean (cleanup). This separates agents that genuinely repaired a system from agents that earned a green check by breaking something else.

## Concepts

- **Infrastructure agent**: an AI agent that operates real systems — diagnosing outages, recovering nodes, repairing storage and databases — rather than editing source files.
- **Layers (L1–L4)**: hardware, local systems, distributed systems, user applications. A benchmark covering only one layer cannot show where an agent's competence stops.
- **Lifecycle**: provisioning, configuration, operation, incident response, and recovery — not only the moment of the fix.
- **Risk**: whether the agent's actions were safe. Destructive shortcuts that satisfy a surface check are penalized rather than rewarded.
- **Effective score**: the difficulty-weighted aggregate reported on the leaderboard, distinct from raw pass rate.
